title: Evaluating mitochondrial length, volume, and cristae ultrastructure in rare mouse adult stem cell populations
protocol: Remove excess media/buffer carefully using a pipette from the well containing isolated EDL myofibers in a 24-well plate.
Wash myofibers with 1 mL of pre-warmed sterile 1× PBS (37°C).
Remove 500 μL of the 1× PBS using a pipette.
Add an equal volume (i.e., 500 μL) of pre-warmed 4% PFA (37°C) to the remaining 1× PBS.
Warm 4% PFA to reduce autofluorescence from the EDL myofiber and improve image resolution.
Incubate myofibers with warmed 4% PFA for 10 min at room temperature with gentle rocking.
Wash myofibers 3 × 5 min with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Store myofibers at 4°C in 1× PBS until further use if not staining cells immediately.
Remove PBS from the samples collected in Part 1, leaving no more than ~100 μL.
Incubate each sample with 1 mL permeabilization solution for 10 min at room temperature with gentle rocking on a plate rocker.
Remove all but ~100 μL of permeabilization solution.
Add 1 mL of blocking solution per sample.
Incubate for 5 h at room temperature on a plate rocker.
Remove all but ∼100 μL of the blocking solution.
Add 100 μL of primary antibody staining solution.
Incubate on a plate rocker overnight at 4°C.
Wash 3 × 5 min in 1 mL of 1× PBS at room temperature on a plate rocker with gentle rocking.
Add 200 μL secondary antibody staining solution.
Incubate with gentle rocking for 1 h at room temperature.
Ensure samples are kept in the dark by wrapping in foil or covering with an opaque container.
Add 200 μL of diluted DAPI for the final 5 min of this incubation.
Wash 3 × 5 min in 1 mL of 1× PBS at room temperature on a plate rocker while gently rocking in dark conditions.
Mount cells/fibers using charged glass slides and Mounting Media.
Create a circle on a charged glass slide using a Pap Pen.
Remove 1× PBS from the sample until about 100–200 μL are left.
Gently pipette the EDL myofibers onto the glass slide with a p1000 pipette.
Allow the EDL myofibers to settle for 2 minutes.
Gently remove excess 1× PBS using a p200 pipette.
Add a thin line of Mounting Media along the center of a rectangular cover slip.
Gently place the coverslip onto the glass slide and press down to create a seal.
Allow slides to dry overnight in the dark at room temperature.
Image mitochondria in adult MuSCs by confocal microscopy.
Place the slide with a drop of immersion oil onto a 63× oil immersion lens.
Locate a cell of interest and center it in the field of view.
Adjust image settings to optimize laser intensity.
Set the pinhole diameter for optimal resolution.
Increase gain to enhance signal strength.
Adjust offset to refine image quality.
Ensure optimal signal-to-noise ratio.
Use Pax7 immunofluorescence to locate MuSCs on EDL myofibers.
Confirm staining of a cell using DAPI.
Use the “Z-Stack” capability of the microscope to capture image slices spanning from the upper to the lower limits of the cells.
Rotate the focus knob in one direction until no mitochondria are visible and set this as the upper limit.
Turn the focus knob in the opposite direction until no mitochondria are visible and set this as the lower limit.
Ensure that all mitochondria in the cell are captured within the established Z-stack limits.
Scan the upper and lower limits of the cell using only the channel with the mitochondrial stain (Tom20 immunofluorescence).
Set each slice at 0.16 μm intervals.
Capture between 20 to 45 slices to ensure all mitochondria within MuSCs residing on EDL myofibers are included.
Acquire optimal Airyscan signal using Zeiss Zen Black 2.3 software.
Enable Airyscan processing in the Tom20 channel.
Adjust microscope settings until a “good” signal is reached.
Capture Z-stack with DAPI, Pax7, and Tom20 channels turned on.
Press the "Start Experiment" button to begin capturing the z-stack.
Process the image using the Airyscan Processing Window.
Select "Airyscan Processing".
Preview the captured image following Airyscan by pressing "Select".
Apply the processing method.
Wait for the Airyscan feature to complete.
Save the processed image in .czi format.
Measure and quantify mitochondrial length using FIJI Software.
Open image in Fiji.
Set “View Stack with” to “hyperstack” and select “autoscale” in the “Bio-Formats Import Options” window.
Select “Image” -> “Stacks” -> “3D Project” from the toolbar to create a 3D projection of the image.
Confirm settings and select “Ok” in the “3D Projection” window.
Adjust the brightness and contrast of the image to better visualize mitochondrial staining.
Go to "Image" > "Adjust" > "Brightness/Contrast".
Adjust the histogram of brightness and contrast.
Click on “Apply” in the “Brightness/Contrast” window to save modifications for all Z-stacks.
Repeat this process for all channels if needed.
Sharpen the image to resolve mitochondria more clearly.
Select the Line Function in the toolbar.
Choose "Freehand" to trace individual mitochondria for subsequent measurement.
Freshly isolate MuSCs from OPA1 WT and OPA1 KO mice.
Show decreased mitochondrial length upon loss of the mitochondrial fusion protein OPA1.
Freshly isolate MuSCs from WT and OPA1 OE mice.
Show increased mitochondrial length upon over-expression of OPA1.
Isolate MuSCs from wild-type mice.
Culture isolated MuSCs for 4 h with or without 2 μm Mdivi-1.
Show increased mitochondrial length upon inhibition of the mitochondrial fission protein DRP1.
Measure mitochondrial volume in Imaris Software (version 9.7.2).
Open the image on Imaris.
Click on the “add new surfaces” button.
Select the Tom20 channel to create a surface over mitochondria.
Do not smooth the image.
Enable background subtraction in the thresholding option.
Measure the width of a single mitochondrion.
Copy the distance measured into the surface creator.
Adjust the thresholding on the histogram for appropriate surface rendering.
Minimize background noise effectively during threshold adjustment.
Enable the “split touching objects” option if individual mitochondria are merged.
Adjust the number of voxels in the histogram to remove background or noise.
Validate the surface rendering for accuracy by the investigator.
Repeat previous steps adjusting background subtraction and thresholding if necessary.
Once the above steps are completed, click “Done” to generate output measures automatically.
To view values, click on “Detailed” in the analysis tab of the software.
Validate extreme values by clicking on them to highlight the product in the rendered surface.
Exclude validated values if they pertain to debris or background staining.
Produce a more appropriate surface of the image if necessary.
Prepare primary muscle stem cells for electron microscopy according to the optimized protocol.
Visualize and quantify mitochondrial ultrastructure via electron microscopy.
This protocol can be adapted for other rare cell populations.
Pellet cells via centrifugation in a 1.5 mL tube at 4,200 rpm for 2 min.
Remove the supernatant using a pipette carefully avoiding the cell pellet.
Gently add 1 ml of sterile 1× PBS.
Centrifuge at 1,200 rpm for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove liquid using a pipette.
Gently add 500 μl of cold EM Fixative.
Incubate for 15 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 5,000 rpm for 8 min.
Remove liquid using a pipette.
Add 500 μl of cold EM Fixative.
Gently resuspend cell pellet in EM Fixative buffer if combining pellets.
Add the resuspended pellet from one tube into the second tube containing another pellet.
Spin the sample at 5,000 rpm for 8 min and remove supernatant.
Prewarm pellets to 37°C in a heating block.
Quickly add 30 μL of low-melt agarose to the cell pellet and gently resuspend.
Spin the mixture at 2,500 rpm for 3 min.
Incubate the agarose embedded pellet at 4°C for 10 min.
Gently loosen the agarose encased pellet from the side of the tube using a sterile stainless steel micro-spatula.
Add 500 μL of EM fixative to ensure the agarose encased pellet is free floating.
Store at 4°C until needed.
Visualize mitochondria in MuSCs via TEM.
Take an image at 1500× magnification to visualize the whole cell of interest.
Take an image at 20,000× magnification to capture mitochondria.
Save TEM images in .dm4 format.
Open the .dm4 image file on Fiji software.
Measure the length of a mitochondrion using the Freehand Line tool.
Count the number of cristae in the mitochondrion.
Measure the width of each cristae using the Freehand Line tool.
Take three measurements for each cristae: one at the top, another in the middle, and one at the bottom.
Calculate the average width of each cristae from the three measurements taken.
Measure the width of the cristae junction between two edges at the base of a cristae.
Perform calculations to determine Cristae # per mitochondria or per mitochondrial length.
Determine the Cristae width.
Calculate the Cristae junction width.
